title: Data Synthesis Using Summary Statistics with Stan
text: vignette demonstrates synthesise delay distribution estimates multiple studies, study reports summary statistics (median, range, IQR, mean ± SD) rather individual observations. approach uses hierarchical Bayesian model implemented Stan. Study-level location parameters drawn shared population distribution, allowing information pooled across studies still accounting -study heterogeneity. Two parametric families compared — log-normal Weibull — using bridge sampling (log marginal likelihood) leave-one-cross-validation (LOO-CV).

title: Simulation Study: Evaluating the Hierarchical Bayesian Model
text: vignette evaluates performance hierarchical Bayesian model across wide range simulated scenarios. study examines well model recovers true population parameters (μ0\mu_0, τ\tau, ϕ\phi) individual observations unavailable summary statistics reported. Three standard parametric families considered — log-normal, Gamma, Weibull — along two extended families: Burr XII Generalised Gamma (GG). Five summary-statistic types evaluated: Note Generalised Gamma identifiability. GG distribution three parameters (μ0\mu_0, ϕ\phi, κ\kappa). hierarchical synthesis setting, certain combinations summary-statistic types sample sizes render shape parameter κ\kappa weakly identified. Scenarios flagged gg_heuristic rule excluded summaries ; scenarios GG judged estimable retained. Performance assessed via: Credible-interval coverage — empirical 95% CI coverage model parameters (μ0\mu_0, τ\tau, ϕ\phi) two predictive quantiles (P50, P95); nominal target: 0.95. Median bias — median (posterior median −- true value) across replicates parameters predictive quantiles; target: 0. Mean absolute error (MAE) — model parameters. Integrated quadratic distance (IQD) Weighted Interval Score (WIS) — measures predictive distribution accuracy; lower better. MCMC convergence rates — proportion replicates R̂<1.05\hat{R} < 1.05.
